editorial.headline: Crude Palm Oil as an Industrial Input
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10431 covers the first industrial transformation of oil-palm fruit into crude palm oil, open nationally to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10431 is about the processing of oil-palm fruit flesh into crude palm oil, or CPO. The record frames this as an upstream industrial activity: the output is still crude, still requiring further processing, and usually used as an input for other activities. That distinction matters. This is not presented as a finished consumer product category, but as the production of a raw industrial oil that sits inside a wider manufacturing chain.

The code is open across every business scale named in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In practical registration terms, that means the activity is not confined to one size of operator in the data supplied here. A small local processor and a large industrial operator may both sit within the same activity description, so long as the registered business is genuinely processing oil-palm fruit flesh into crude palm oil that remains subject to further processing.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clear. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership figure in the record is 100%. The source given for that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no partial ceiling to interpret and no separate condition to infer from the slim record. On the national reading alone, this is a foreign-open industrial activity.

The Bali picture is also unusually clean. The record does include Bali’s island-wide moratorium rule, which blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. But this activity is not marked as blocked in Bali. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. So the honest conclusion is not that Bali adds a hidden percentage cap, quota, or local-partner condition; the record says no such thing. For this code, the national openness and the Bali-side status point in the same direction: foreign-owned registration is not blocked by the Bali moratorium on the facts supplied.
